newsitem.title: USA: Huntway seeks consent for restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Huntway seeks consent for restructuring.

text.p: Huntway Partners LP said Friday it has begun the process of gaining unitholder and creditor approval for its financial restructuring.
Upon winning consent for its recapitalization, Huntway said it plans to enter a prepackaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy for final confirmation.

"The prepackaged plan provides for the continuing and timely payment in full of all Huntway's obligation to suppliers, other trade creditors and employees under normal trade terms," the company said in a statement.
Huntway previously announced four of five senior lenders, comprising about 86 percent of its senior debt, consented to the plan, but the other 14-percent holder did not.
Two junior debtholders have also approved the plan.
The restructuring reduces total debt outstanding by over $68.8 million and cuts accrued unpaid interest by about $2.4 million.
The plan provides for the issuance of around 13.8 million new units to lenders and warrant holders, which will boost total units outstanding to 25.3 million from 11.6 million.
In addition, the plan provides that current options to purchase 546,059 common units will remain outstanding.

It calls for the issuance of new options to acquire over 3.4 million common units. It requires the cancellation of current options to purchase 1.0 common units, as well as the cancellation of warrants to acquire 3.3 million current units.

If completed total units outstanding on a fully diluted basis will increase initially to 29.3 million from roughly 16.5 million. Total debt and accrued interest will decline by a combined $71,143,000 as of September 30, 1996.
The plan also provides for certain potential issuances of units and options in the future.
